messages.subject: Sharing faceting variable between datasets
parts:
Hopefully this will be obvious to someone else, because it seems a reasonable thing to do but I can't figure out how to make it work.

I have two datasets, one with counts of moths from pheromone traps, and another with dates of cold fronts, covering two field seasons (years).  I want to plot regular lines for the moth counts, and vertical lines on the date of each cold front passage, faceted by year.  I can get most of the way there using x=doy (day of year).  What I can't figure out is how to get the faceting to recognize that the faceting variable is the same in each dataset.  This code shows a couple of attempts to put in geom_vline parameters to do that, but neither works.  Both versions try to plot all the values in the front dataset, not just for the "year" in the current facet.

If this is possible, please let me know how. Thanks!
Jennifer

parts:
Jennifer, 

If I'm not mistaken, you seem to have had it already. I emptied the ggplot() and put that information directly into the geom_line() then changed x to xintercept for geom_vline(). 

It looks like it's doing what you want... 
ggplot () +
geom_vline(data = all.fronts, aes(xintercept = doy)) +
geom_line(data = cewall, aes(x = doy, y = avgmoths, color=variable)) +

Unless, I'm not understanding what you want? 

Thanks for including example data and reproducible plotting code.

Brandon

On Saturday, November 7, 2015 at 3:30:01 PM UTC-6, Brandon Hurr wrote:

Jennifer, 

If I'm not mistaken, you seem to have had it already. I emptied the ggplot() and put that information directly into the geom_line() then changed x to xintercept for geom_vline(). 

It looks like it's doing what you want... 
ggplot () +
geom_vline(data = all.fronts, aes(xintercept = doy)) +
geom_line(data = cewall, aes(x = doy, y = avgmoths, color=variable)) +
facet_grid (year~., scales = "free_y")



Unless, I'm not understanding what you want? 

Thanks for including example data and reproducible plotting code.

Brandon

On Sat, Nov 7, 2015 at 11:52 AM, Jennifer Krauel <unquench...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hopefully this will be obvious to someone else, because it seems a reasonable thing to do but I can't figure out how to make it work.

I have two datasets, one with counts of moths from pheromone traps, and another with dates of cold fronts, covering two field seasons (years).  I want to plot regular lines for the moth counts, and vertical lines on the date of each cold front passage, faceted by year.  I can get most of the way there using x=doy (day of year).  What I can't figure out is how to get the faceting to recognize that the faceting variable is the same in each dataset.  This code shows a couple of attempts to put in geom_vline parameters to do that, but neither works.  Both versions try to plot all the values in the front dataset, not just for the "year" in the current facet.

If this is possible, please let me know how. Thanks!
Jennifer
